entryRequirements.passportValidity: Use a passport valid for at least 6 months beyond arrival where possible.
entryRequirements.visaSummary: Australian passport holders can generally visit Hong Kong visa-free for short stays, but should confirm the current permitted stay and any onward travel expectations.
entryRequirements.arrivalCardOrDeclaration: Check whether any digital health, customs, or arrival declarations apply for your travel dates.
entryRequirements.officialSourceNote: Review Hong Kong Immigration Department guidance before departure.
importantNotes: Keep onward travel details and accommodation information accessible.
Rules for onward travel into mainland China are separate and should be checked independently.

handyPhrases.context: A friendly Cantonese greeting, though English is common in many business settings.
M goi is often used for service or small favours; doh jeh is more for gifts or bigger thanks.
Useful when asking about stored-value transit payment options.

businessEtiquette.summary: Hong Kong business culture often values speed, preparation, and direct but polished communication.
tips: Be punctual and assume meetings will move quickly.
Have numbers or next steps ready rather than staying too high-level.
Smart business dress still tends to read well in formal settings.

foodAndPracticalities.tapWater: Tap water is treated, but many visitors still prefer filtered or bottled water.
foodAndPracticalities.tipping: Many restaurants add a service charge, so extra tipping is modest or optional.
foodAndPracticalities.dietaryNotes: Vegetarian options are improving, though menus may still need a quick clarification on broth, seafood, or pork.
foodAndPracticalities.commonFoodTips: Dim sum, cha chaan teng cafes, and noodle shops are practical everyday options, but queues can move quickly and seating can be tight.

moneyAndPayments.cardAcceptance: Cards are widely accepted in hotels, malls, and many restaurants.
moneyAndPayments.cashNotes: Keep some cash for smaller food shops, markets, and older taxis, though mobile and stored-value payments are common.
moneyAndPayments.tipping: Often limited to rounding up or a small extra amount if service charge is not included.
roughCostExamples: Milk tea or coffee: about HKD 20 to 35
Simple noodle or rice meal: about HKD 45 to 90
Airport Express to Central: about HKD 100
